text:
alex: Quick sync — proposing we shrink the three-mode seam to a minimal runtime-facing surface so adapters only translate a tiny manifest and auth token. The idea: one canonical request shape, adapters map to infra specifics. Thoughts? :thinking:

maria: Love the intent. Main worry is auth/keys lifecycle — private needs KMS/HSM flows and hosted uses Redwood KMS. How do adapters expose key rotation and audit hooks without leaking complexity upstream?

sam: Also telemetry. If adapters shape requests differently we risk losing per-tenant latency attribution and token-level cost breakdowns. We need invariant fields for tracing and billing.

devops-bot: Deploy queued: staging/adapter-slimdown v0.1 -> rolling. CI: 1/3 passed, 2/3 flaky tests (timeout on kvcache).

ajex: (typo) alex: +1 on invariant fields. Proposed minimal invariants: tenant_id, request_id, model_version, trace_context, billing_profile. Adapters may add metadata but these five are required.

jess: For fallback semantics we should keep an explicit "compatibility intent" header so control plane can instruct runtime to fall back to cheaper model variants when dedicated pool is full. Example header: X-RW-Intent: degrade_to_variant=v_low_cost

kai: If we standardize a tiny manifest, here's a rough shape we could use (adapter translates into infra ops):
```
manifest_version: v1
tenant_id: T-123
runtime: hosted|dedicated|private
model: gpt-3x
qos: { latency_slo_ms: 200, burst: 50 }
auth: { token_ref: k8s-secret://name, kms_key: arn:... }
observability: { sampling: 0.1, trace_key: request_id }
```
Keep it intentionally small.

sre-oncall: Important: eviction/eviction-reason must be implicit in the runtime responses and surfaced to control-plane logs. If dedicated evicts for maintenance we need deterministic fallback routing and TTL for cached KV entries. How do adapters signal that?

alex: Suggest adapters implement a small status endpoint /adapter-status that returns JSON (status, allowed_fallbacks, maintenance_window). Control plane polls and records evictions. That keeps runtime decisions local but observable.

maria: That helps. For private we also need an out-of-band audit sink option (s3/syslog) because customers may want on-prem copy of audit logs. Add optional 'audit_endpoint' to manifest.

sam: For telemetry invariants, I propose we add "billing_profile" to the manifest and require adapters to emit a normalized telemetry envelope to a common collector endpoint. If adapter can't push, it should return a telemetry hint in the response for the control plane to scrape.

jess: One more tradeoff: do we let adapters mutate prompts for quantization/cost reasons? If yes, need strong explicit consent and a signature on the original prompt for auditability.

kai: We could support an opt-in transform pipeline with an audit header: X-RW-Transform: qz-v1; signature:sha256(...). If transform disabled, adapters must be passthrough.

sre-oncall: SLA implications: any adapter-side transform or fallback must include a deterministic latency budget so control plane can account for retry windows. Otherwise SLO math breaks.

alex: Agreed. Action items: (1) I'll draft an RFC that defines the 5 invariants + manifest v1 + /adapter-status contract. (2) @maria please draft KMS/hsm lifecycle constraints for private vs hosted. (3) @sam please propose the telemetry envelope format (one pager). (4) @jess + @kai work a minimal transform audit header proposal.

maria: On it. Expect a short doc by EOD Friday.

sam: I'll sketch telemetry tomorrow AM.

jess: I'll pair with kai later today. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Reminder: staging testing still flaky. Please don't block RFC for e2e green — we can dogfood behind a feature flag.

alex: Good call. RFC will include a feature-flagged rollout plan and a small compatibility test matrix. Plan to post RFC next week. Thanks everyone.
